name: Saint Martin's Island
description: The only coral reef island in Bangladesh, famous for crystal blue waters, coconut groves, and Chera Dwip.

name: Inani Beach & Marine Drive
description: World's longest marine drive hugging golden sandy beaches, green hills, and coral stone shores.

name: Himchari National Park
description: Famous for hills overlooking the Bay of Bengal, lush canopy, and seasonal waterfalls.

name: Nilgiri Resort & Hilltop
description: One of the highest hill peaks in Bangladesh where you can touch floating white clouds.

name: Nilachal (Tiger Hill)
description: Breathtaking panoramic view of Bandarban town and golden sunsets from high mountain cliffs.

name: Boga Lake
description: A mysterious high-altitude natural volcanic crater lake situated 1,500 feet above sea level on the way to Keokradong.

name: Keokradong Peak
description: One of the highest mountain peaks in Bangladesh offering the ultimate trekking adventure.

name: Nafakhum Waterfall
description: Referred to as the 'Niagara of Bengal', an awe-inspiring wild waterfall on the Remakri river.

name: Sajek Valley
description: The 'Kingdom of Clouds' perched atop the lush hills of Rangamati, accessed via Khagrachhari.

name: Kaptai Lake & Hanging Bridge
description: The largest man-made lake in South Asia surrounded by forested hills and native boat rides.

name: Alutila Cave & Risang Waterfall
description: Mysterious 100-meter dark stone cave that you cross holding flaming torches, plus nearby cascades.

name: Patenga Sea Beach & Naval Beach
description: Vibrant shoreline at the confluence of the Karnaphuli River and Bay of Bengal, famous for spicy fried crabs.

name: Chandranath Hill & Temple
description: Scenic pilgrimage peak in Sitakunda standing at 1,150 feet with lush trekking trails and waterfalls.

name: Guliakhali Sea Beach
description: Known as Muradpur beach; unique blend of green grass lawn meadows interwoven with ocean waterways.

name: Shalban Vihara & Mainamati
description: Ancient 8th-century Buddhist monastery archaeological site with terracotta plaques and museum.

name: Lalbagh Fort
description: Iconic 17th-century Mughal fort complex housing Pari Bibi's tomb, the hammam khana, and Mughal gardens.

name: Ahsan Manzil (Pink Palace)
description: The majestic former official palace of the Nawabs of Dhaka on the banks of the Buriganga River.

name: National Parliament (Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban)
description: Louis Kahn's world-renowned architectural masterpiece surrounded by an artificial lake and lush lawns.

name: Panam City & Sonargaon
description: Ancient historic capital of Bengal with beautifully preserved 19th-century colonial mansions and Folk Art Museum.

name: Bangabandhu Safari Park
description: Largest safari park in South Asia with roaming lions, tigers, giraffes, zebras, and aviary birds.

name: Nikli Haor
description: Vast ocean-like freshwater wetland where traditional wooden boats sail across endless blue waters.

name: Mohera Jamindar Bari
description: Stunning European-style palace complex with manicured gardens, ponds, and ornate Corinthian pillars.

name: Padma Bridge Viewpoint
description: Bangladesh's pride — a 6.15 km monumental multi-purpose bridge across the mighty Padma River.

name: Ratargul Swamp Forest
description: Only freshwater swamp forest in Bangladesh; explore submerged evergreen trees by quiet wooden canoes.

name: Jaflong & Zero Point
description: Where the Dawki River flows from Meghalaya into Bangladesh, surrounded by stone beds and tea hills.

name: Bholaganj Sada Pathor
description: Icy crystal clear spring waters cascading over sparkling white limestone pebbles at the border.

name: Bichnakandi
description: Surreal meeting point of seven hill streams with waterfalls pouring down from lush Meghalaya mountains.

name: Hazrat Shah Jalal Mazar Sharif
description: Revered 14th-century Sufi saint shrine with holy koi fish pond and historical relics in heart of Sylhet.

name: Lawachara National Park
description: Lush tropical semi-evergreen rainforest home to the endangered Western Hoolock Gibbons and scenic train tracks.

name: Madhabkunda Waterfall
description: The highest single-drop waterfall in Bangladesh dropping 200 feet amidst deep tea estate hills.

name: Sreemangal Tea Estates
description: The 'Tea Capital of Bangladesh' with endless rolling green tea terraces, 7-layer tea, and pineapple farms.

name: Tanguar Haor & Barek Tila
description: UNESCO Ramsar wetland site famous for magical houseboat cruises on turquoise waters and Shimul Bagan.

name: Sundarbans National Park (Kotka & Karamjal)
description: World's largest tidal halophytic mangrove forest and UNESCO World Heritage site, home of the Royal Bengal Tiger.

name: Sixty Dome Mosque (Shat Gombuj Masjid)
description: 15th-century UNESCO World Heritage architectural triumph built by Khan Jahan Ali with 77 domes and 60 pillars.

name: Lalon Shah Mazar
description: Spiritual sanctuary of mystic philosopher and Baul king Fakir Lalon Shah at Chheuriya.

name: Rabindranath Tagore Shilaidaha Kuthibari
description: Country house where Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore lived and penned immortal poems including Gitanjali.

name: Mujibnagar Memorial Complex
description: Historic birthplace of independent Bangladesh government where the first oath was taken in 1971.

name: Kuakata Sea Beach (Daughter of Ocean)
description: Unique 18 km continuous beach from where you can witness both panoramic sunrise and sunset over the sea.

name: Bhimruli Floating Guava Market
description: Bangladesh's 'Venice of Bengal' where hundreds of boats gather daily selling fresh green guavas on narrow canals.

name: Char Kukri Mukri Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Secluded island sanctuary with spotted deer, migratory bird flocks, mangroves, and virgin sands.

name: Paharpur Somapura Mahavihara
description: UNESCO World Heritage site: second largest Buddhist monastery south of the Himalayas dating back to 8th century.

name: Mahasthangarh & Behula Lakshmindar Basor Ghar
description: Oldest fortified archaeological city in Bangladesh (3rd century BC Pundranagara) along the Karatoya River.

name: Puthia Temple Complex
description: Largest cluster of historic terracotta Hindu temples in Bangladesh including Govinda Temple and Shiva Temple.

name: Padma Riverbank & T-Groin (Rajshahi)
description: Serene riverside promenade famous for breathtaking sunsets over the golden sands of the Padma River.

name: Uttara Gonobhaban (Dighapatia Palace)
description: Majestic 18th-century royal palace of the Maharajas of Dighapatia, featuring grand Italian clock tower and gardens.

name: Kantajew Temple (Kantanagar)
description: Magnificent 18th-century navaratna terracotta temple, acclaimed as the finest terracotta architecture in Bengal.

name: Tetulia & Kanchenjunga View Point
description: Northernmost tip of Bangladesh where the snow-capped Himalayan peak of Mount Kanchenjunga glows at sunrise.

name: Tajhat Palace
description: Grand classical Roman-inspired royal palace built by Maharaja Kumar Gopal Lal Roy in early 20th century.

name: Birishiri & Shusong Durgapur Ceramic Lake
name_bn: বিরিশিরি ও সুসং দুর্গাপুর চীনামাটির হ্রদ
description: Famous for the turquoise blue china clay ceramic lake nestled beside white clay hills and Someshwari River.

name: Shashi Lodge
description: Splendid European neoclassical palace of the Muktagacha zamindars with the famous Venus marble fountain.
